I've been working recently on robust statistics (in adversarial machine learning), and I've stumbled on a 2-category (I think), which should be well-known around here. Let me first motivate the structure with the original problem.

The original example

Consider an euclidean space XXX and the space P2(X)P_2(X)P2​(X) of probability distributions with finite variance. Assume there is a true distribution η†\eta_\daggerη†​, but an adversary AAA contaminates η†\eta_\daggerη†​ and you only get to observe a distribution μ\muμ such that (1−p)η†≤μ(1-p) \eta_\dagger \le \mu(1−p)η†​≤μ. The goal is to estimate the mean mη†m_{\eta_\dagger}mη†​​ of the true distribution.

In our formulation, we choose a gauge, i.e. a (lsc) function

ℓ(x,η)={∥x−mη∥2ση2if ση2>00if ση2=0 and x=mη+∞if ση2=0 and x≠mη\ell(x,\eta) = \begin{cases} \frac{\lVert x - m_\eta \rVert^2}{\sigma^2_\eta} &\text{if } \sigma^2_\eta > 0 \\ 0 &\text{if } \sigma^2_\eta = 0 \text{ and } x = m_\eta \\ +\infty &\text{if } \sigma^2_\eta = 0 \text{ and } x \ne m_\eta \end{cases}ℓ(x,η)=⎩⎨⎧​ση2​∥x−mη​∥2​0+∞​if ση2​>0if ση2​=0 and x=mη​if ση2​=0 and x=mη​​

that prices the estimation xxx against the truth. An defense gives a set D(μ)D(\mu)D(μ) of candidates xxx.
The defense DDD is κ\kappaκ-robust against AAA if

∀μ,∀x∈D(μ),∀η∈A⊤(μ),ℓ(x,η)≤κ\forall \mu, \forall x\in D(\mu), \forall \eta \in A^\top(\mu), \ell(x, \eta) \le \kappa∀μ,∀x∈D(μ),∀η∈A⊤(μ),ℓ(x,η)≤κ

where A⊤(μ)A^\top(\mu)A⊤(μ) denotes the set of admissible distributions η\etaη, (1−p)η≤μ(1-p)\eta \le \mu(1−p)η≤μ.
The least of such κ\kappaκ defines the robustness coefficient

κ(ℓ,A,D)=sup⁡μsup⁡x∈D(μ)sup⁡η∈A⊤(μ)ℓ(x,η)\kappa(\ell, A, D) = \sup_\mu \sup_{x \in D(\mu)} \sup_{\eta \in A^\top(\mu)} \ell(x,\eta)κ(ℓ,A,D)=μsup​x∈D(μ)sup​η∈A⊤(μ)sup​ℓ(x,η)

Notice that in this example, the adversary AAA can be represented as a relation A(η,μ)A(\eta,\mu)A(η,μ) stating whether the candidate η\etaη is admissible with respect to the observed μ\muμ. Similarly, we are looking for defenses DDD that are relations: D(x,μ)D(x,\mu)D(x,μ) holds iff xxx is a valid estimate with respect to the observed μ\muμ.

Our work focuses on computing the robustness coefficient for various defenses, adversaries, gauges, etc.
We quickly realize that having ways to combine defenses, adversaries and gauges, and derive the robustness coefficients would be useful.

2-categorical formulation

Let V=([0,+∞],min⁡,+)V = ([0,+\infty], \min, +)V=([0,+∞],min,+) denote the tropical rig. I am considering a 2-category VVV-mat of matrices valued in VVV

  • objects are sets
  • arrows ℓ:X→Y\ell : X \to Yℓ:X→Y are matrices, i.e. function ℓ:Y×X→V\ell : Y \times X \to Vℓ:Y×X→V, composition being

(D∘A)(x,μ)=inf⁡η(D(x,η)+A(η,μ))(D \circ A)(x,\mu) = \inf_\eta (D(x,\eta) + A(\eta,\mu))(D∘A)(x,μ)=ηinf​(D(x,η)+A(η,μ))

  • 2-cells: ℓ⇒ℓ′\ell \Rightarrow \ell'ℓ⇒ℓ′ is a nonegative real κ\kappaκ such that ℓ+κ≥ℓ′\ell + \kappa \ge \ell'ℓ+κ≥ℓ′ entrywise. The least such κ\kappaκ defines a (Lawvere) metric between parallel matrices

d(ℓ,ℓ′)=inf⁡{κ  :  ℓ+κ≥ℓ′}d(\ell, \ell') = \inf \{ \kappa \;:\; \ell + \kappa \ge \ell' \}d(ℓ,ℓ′)=inf{κ:ℓ+κ≥ℓ′}

Relations can be encoded as "hard" matrices whose entries are {0,+∞}\{0,+\infty\}{0,+∞}. So hard adversaries and defenses can be represented as arrows in VVV-mat.

Now the fun part,

  • a gauge is a matrix ℓ:L→R\ell : L \to Rℓ:L→R from the "latent" set to the "response" set RRR
  • an adversary is a matrix A:L→OA : L \to OA:L→O from the latent set to the "observation" set OOO
  • a defense is a matrix D:O→RD : O \to RD:O→R from the observation set to the response set

When AAA and DDD represent hard adversary and defense, it turns out the following are equivalent

  • DDD is κ\kappaκ-robust against AAA
  • κ\kappaκ witnesses a 2-cell D∘A⇒ℓD \circ A \Rightarrow \ellD∘A⇒ℓ, i.e. D∘A+κ≥ℓD \circ A + \kappa \ge \ellD∘A+κ≥ℓ.

This generalizes obviously to any matrices A,DA,DA,D.

Interestingly, the right extension ℓA\ell^AℓA of ℓ\ellℓ along AAA is the best (soft) defense, because of the adjunction

d(D∘A,ℓ)=d(D,ℓA)d(D \circ A, \ell) = d(D, \ell^A)d(D∘A,ℓ)=d(D,ℓA)

The robust statistics game then becomes an issue of finding hard-approximations of ℓA\ell^AℓA. And the compositional nature of all this gives rules to compute robustness coefficients (which are just metric distances between parallel matrices).

Questions

  • Is my formulation of VVV-matrices as a 2-category correct?
  • Are you aware of similar work? i.e., applying this kind of matrices to robust statistics? or any other field with similar interests?

Thank you.
